newsitem.title: USA: JLG Industries mulls workforce reductions.
newsitem.headline: JLG Industries mulls workforce reductions.

text.p: JLG Industries said Monday that last week it provided 60-day notice to employees of possible workforce reductions at its McConnellsburg boom lift plant and it two scissor lift factories in Bedford, Pa.
The company said the notices were provided to comply with federal law, which requires 60-day notice for reductions in force of more than 500 workers.
JLG also said that it has scheduled a two-day plant shutdown in July and a two-week shutdown in August.

In a statement, chief executive officer L. David Black said, "We have been contemplating some workforce reductions as a result of recent order softness. We have not yet determined the extent of the layoffs or their financial impact." He added that the notice was given to preserve the company's flexibility to respond to market conditions.
JLG makes aerial work platforms for use in the industrial, commercial, institutional and construction markets.
